title: HSA shared definitions
description: Shared building blocks referenced by the HSA v1 document contracts. This file is NOT a document kind: it has no $hsa_kind discriminator and no HSA document ever validates against it directly. It exists so identity, timestamp, timeframe, provenance, parameter and output-contract shapes have exactly one definition across the contract set.

strategy_id.description: Stable canonical strategy identity. Shared verbatim with CER (PID lines 162-171). Never reused for a different strategy and never changed across versions.

semver.description: Strict MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Promoted versions are immutable (PID lines 185-189): a modification is a new version, never an edit in place.

utc_timestamp.description: RFC3339 instant that MUST be expressed in UTC with a literal trailing Z. Local time is display-only and never persisted (PID line 225).

timeframe.description: Chart timeframe. Suffix M means MINUTES (per PID line 95, which writes 1H/15M/5M/1M), H hours, D days, W weeks. There is deliberately no month suffix, so M is never ambiguous. Examples: 5M, 15M, 1H, 4H, 1D.

timeframe_role.description: Semantic timeframe role (PID lines 84-97). The ROLE set is canonical; the timeframe each role maps to is not, so 4H/1H/15M/5M and 1D/4H/1H/15M are both legal mappings.

direction_semantics.description: How direction is derived and expressed. Required everywhere direction can be observed (PID lines 74, 136).

source_type.description: Supported intake sources, one per PID lines 102-108.

provenance.description: Traceability back to the original strategy source (PID line 145). Provenance is mandatory: an HSA artefact whose origin cannot be named is not governed.

hermes_field.description: One measurable market fact this artefact consumes from HERMES (PID lines 21-22, 53, 132). HSA maps requirements onto HERMES outputs; it never invents its own feed.

parameter.description: A tunable parameter with an explicit default, allowed range and units (PID line 140). Exactly one of allowed_range or allowed_values must be present, so every parameter has a mechanically checkable domain.

units.description: Physical or logical unit, for example bars, pips, ratio, percent, count. Use the literal none for dimensionless parameters.

output_contract.description: The normalised output shape FORGE implements (PID lines 61, 141, 148). Normalisation is what makes composition possible without strategies knowing about each other.

signal_type.description: BOOLEAN: matched or not. STATE: a named state from a declared set. SCORE: a bounded numeric strength.

reason_field.description: Name of the output field carrying the human-readable reason for the result. Mandatory so a chain can build its own explicit match/non-match reason (PID line 80) out of its components.

cer_reference_type.description: What HSA records or targets through CER contracts, one per PID lines 175-179.

criterion.description: A machine-evaluable acceptance or rejection criterion. Prose alone is not sufficient: FORGE and CER must be able to evaluate it without interpretation (PID line 148).
